# Flowzora

> Flowzora is a workflow automation agency working with small and mid-sized
> businesses worldwide. We connect the tools a company already runs, remove the
> manual steps between them, and hand over systems the client owns outright.

Flowzora operates as a specialist agency under oneProductLab. It was founded by
Niraj Kumar, a backend and AI engineer whose background is in production APIs,
data platforms and applied machine learning, with earlier machine learning
research work at C-DAC.

## What we do

- Sales and revenue operations: lead capture, routing, enrichment, CRM hygiene
- Marketing and lifecycle automation: segmentation, hand-offs, reporting
- Internal operations and back-office: onboarding, approvals, reconciliation
- Customer support automation: triage, classification, drafted responses
- Integrations and data plumbing: reliable, observable syncs between systems
- AI agents and assisted workflows: used only where a rule cannot express the task

## Pricing

- Automation Audit — from $500, 1 to 2 weeks. A map of one workflow, a number on
  what it is costing, and a fixed quote. Credited in full against a build.
- First System — quoted after the Audit. One workflow built and handed over, at a
  fixed price agreed in writing, with 90 days of fixes included after handover.
- Operations Partner — from $1,500 per month, ongoing.

Build pricing is deliberately not published: scope varies from a few days to
several weeks, so a general figure would be a guess. The Audit fee is published
because it is the one number that can be stated honestly in advance.

## How we describe our evidence

Published projects are labeled exactly for what they are: "client" or
"internal-build". We do not publish client logos, named customers
or performance metrics we cannot substantiate. If a page does not name a client,
no client engagement is being claimed.

Client testimonials on the site are public LinkedIn recommendations, quoted
verbatim and linked to the profile that wrote them, with the relationship
(client or colleague) stated on each.

## Reference answers

**What does workflow automation cost?** An Automation Audit starts at $500 and is
credited in full against the build. The build itself is quoted after the Audit,
because one workflow can be a few days or several weeks of work — a number given
before anyone has looked at the process is a guess. Ongoing support starts at
$1,500 per month. Expect 10 to 20% of build cost per year in maintenance once the
included 90 days ends.

**What happens after handover?** Every build includes 90 days of maintenance at
no extra cost: breakages and upstream API changes are fixed by us. After that the
client can maintain it themselves — they own the code and runbooks — or move to
an ongoing Operations Partner engagement.

**How long does it take?** Three to five weeks for one workflow, including
mapping. Working automation appears in the first two weeks, not at the end.

**Who owns the result?** The client. Code, credentials and infrastructure are in
their name from day one, and handover includes runbooks and diagrams.

**When is an AI agent the right tool?** Only when a task needs judgment a rule
cannot express — classification, extraction or drafting. Rules are preferred
wherever the logic can be written down, because they are cheaper and predictable.

**Which platforms do you build on?** Zapier, Make, n8n or custom services,
chosen per workflow. Platforms where they genuinely fit; code where reliability,
testing or volume demands it. We are not tied to one vendor or language.

**What is included after handover?** 90 days of maintenance on every build, plus
runbooks, diagrams and full ownership of code and credentials.
